key_concepts: Some materials such as iron, nickel, and steel are magnetic
Materials like rubber, wood, plastic, cotton, copper, and aluminum are non-magnetic
Magnets have an invisible magnetic field
The ends of a magnet are called poles
Magnetic poles exert a force that can pull together or push apart
The push and pull of a magnet is called magnetism
Magnets do not attract all metals
Magnetic force is strongest between the two poles
The magnetic field surrounds the magnet, not only the South Pole
Same poles repel while unlike poles attract
Magnetic field lines are closer near the poles and farther away from the magnet
Closer magnetic field lines indicate a stronger magnetic field
